title: Choose the visual world
question: Replacing the dashboard's visual world. The roll assigned Wing & Bay. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Wing & Bay
options.lineage: Hospital wayfinding supergraphics — Aicher, Vignelli, Crosby/Fletcher/Forbes
options.thesis: A backend read the way you read your way through a hospital: supergraphic bay numerals, departmental colour fields, plates and arrows at architectural scale.
options.viewport: A hung corridor sign across the top: building name left, four destination plates with colour chips and arrows, live status right. Beneath it the wing entrance — a supergraphic 01 in vermilion bleeding off its field, SERVICE VITALS set in condensed caps beside it, bay code SVC-001 on a door plate. Then four bay-number readouts (uptime, heap, Postgres round-trip, active records) as huge mono numerals on a hairline-ruled band, and the latency trace as a flat wall-mounted graph plate.
options.risk: Signage colour can slide into institutional dullness or cheerful medical mint; supergraphic numerals eat a phone viewport unless the wing entrance collapses to a colour band.

options.label: Midnight Interchange
options.lineage: Metropolitan rail diagram as midnight-blue enamel mural
options.thesis: The architecture as a transit network: layers are stations in fixed order, module boundaries are fare boundaries, a request is a traced route.
options.viewport: A full-bleed enamel mural: four coloured lines bending at 45° and 90°, the selected line burning brightest, interchange circles blooming where modules meet. route → controller → service → repository → Prisma runs as five stations along one corridor.
options.case: Fuses strongly — the layer stack becomes station order and enforced boundaries become fare boundaries, which is more legible than the prose it replaces. Loses on product clarity: a network mural has no native grammar for a paged, sorted directory of patient records or a raw JSON response body, so two of four panels would need invented grammar.
options.risk: A diagram world flatters the architecture panel and fights the two data-table panels.

options.label: Depot Blind
options.lineage: Bus depot destination blind — dyed duck cloth on a roll
options.thesis: Status as a roll of stacked cloth courses stepping under one fixed window; a fault is the row halted mid-step, two half-legends meeting across one seam.
options.viewport: Bottle-green cloth drenching the field, lit from behind so the weave shows. Chrome-yellow condensed caps step one whole line-height with an overshoot whenever a telemetry value changes; the lead panel alone inverts to dark-on-pale.
options.case: The best fault state on the table — a row stopped mid-step across a single seam is original and unmistakable, and the snap-step motion makes live values genuinely physical. Loses on product clarity: one type size, caps only, and controls that take no dye break the seven-field patient registration form, the response viewer, and the boundary-rule prose.
options.risk: Its own grammar forbids the type hierarchy and dyed controls that three of the four panels need.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.lineage: CRT oscilloscope on a signal bench
options.thesis: Every reading measured against a ten-division etched graticule, with detented knobs for timebase and trigger.
options.viewport: Postgres round-trip riding as a persistent phosphor trace across a square ten-division graticule, poll interval as a detented timebase knob, seven-segment readouts in amber when armed.
options.case: Instrumentation is this audience's true home and the latency trace would be native and beautiful. Fuses poorly overall: a scope has no grammar at all for a paged directory of twenty patient records, and phosphor-green on near-black glass is precisely the near-black-plus-one-neon observability rut this redesign exists to leave.
options.risk: Lands in the exact category default the request asked to remove, and covers only one of four panels.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The observability dashboard every backend ships: near-black ground, one cyan accent, glass metric tiles, gradient sparklines — executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: A 4-up row of glass metric cards with big glowing numbers, a gradient area chart beneath, a zinc-bordered table below, and a subtle dot grid behind everything.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other backend dashboard, including the one this replaces.
